questions.q: Why does China's growing appetite for meat matter to the whole world?
a: Its huge population means its farming trends spread globally
It exports most of its meat to poorer countries
It has banned traditional farming methods outright
It produces more meat than every other nation combined
questions.why: Lesson 1 says changes in China reach the rest of the planet because of its size.

questions.q: What does the summary call the easiest step anyone can take right now?
a: Waste less of the food already being bought
Switch entirely to a plant-based diet
Buy only imported meat products
Avoid eating at restaurants
questions.why: Lesson 2 says cutting food waste would free enough resources to feed the world.

questions.q: Which two labels does the summary recommend looking for on meat?
a: Grass-fed and pasture-raised
Farm-fresh and all-natural
Lean and low-fat
Premium and family-owned
questions.why: Lesson 3 says these labels show the animals ate grass, while the others are meaningless.

questions.q: Why is traditional farming described as more sustainable?
a: Cows eat grass people cannot, and the soil stays fertile naturally
It relies on fewer workers and much larger fields
It ships food across the world more efficiently
It uses more grain but produces tastier meat
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that natural cycles replenish the land instead of depleting it.

questions.q: How does the summary say consumers can change the food industry?
a: By spending money and voicing complaints according to their values
By waiting for governments to pass stricter farming laws
By refusing to buy any food that carries a label
By eating less often and skipping breakfast
questions.why: Lesson 3 argues the industry supplies what buyers demand, so each purchase counts.
